speaker: Sheldon
text: Penny. Penny. Penny. It's 11 a.m.

speaker: Penny
text: Hey, Sheldon. I know, you're safe.

speaker: Sheldon
text: This package came while you were at work.

speaker: Penny
text: Oh, great, my rhinestones, thank you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Excuse me. You have to sign this.

speaker: Penny
text: What is it?

speaker: Sheldon
text: When I signed for the package, I was deputized by the United Parcel Service and entrusted with its final delivery. I now need you to acknowledge receipt of the package so that I'm fully indemnified and no longer liable.

speaker: Penny
text: Sheldon, it's just a box of rhinestones.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, the contents are irrelevant. A legal bailment has been created. Does that mean nothing to you?

speaker: Penny
text: It means nothing to anybody. Come here, let me show you what I'm doing.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Bailment describes a relationship in common law where a physical possession of personal property or chattels is transferred from one person, the bailer, to another person, the bailkee.

speaker: Penny
text: Look, look, look, I started a business.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Obviously not a cleaning business.

speaker: Penny
text: No, I'm making flower barrettes, see? I called them Penny Blossoms. I made one for myself, and then all the girls at work wanted one, and then I showed some to this lady who runs a shop in Old Town. She sells cards and homemade jewelry. She said she wanted to sell them. I said okay, and in one week I made a hundred and fifty-six dollars.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Good for you. Sign here.

speaker: Penny
text: Sheldon, don't you get it? If this takes off, I won't have to be a waitress anymore.

speaker: Sheldon
text: But then who will bring me my cheeseburger on Tuesday nights? What's her name?

speaker: Penny
text: Another waitress?

speaker: Penny
text: I don't know.

speaker: Sheldon
text: And you're going to let her handle my food?

speaker: Penny
text: Nancy, her name is Nancy.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I think you're just making that up.

speaker: Penny
text: Sheldon, I'm sorry about your hamburger, okay? I just don't want to be a waitress for the rest of my life.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Cheeseburger, I get a cheeseburger. Maybe I'd be better off with Nancy.

speaker: Penny
text: Fine, cheeseburger.

speaker: Penny
text: So, what do you think? I mean, this could be a business, right?

speaker: Sheldon
text: How many of these can you make a day? And how much profit do you make per Penny Blossom?

speaker: Penny
text: About twenty.

speaker: Penny
text: I don't know, like fifty cents, I'm not sure.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, of course you're not, all right. Ten dollars a day times five days a week times fifty-two weeks a year is two thousand six hundred dollars. Before taxes.

speaker: Penny
text: That's all? Well, I don't have to pay taxes on this stuff.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I believe the Internal Revenue Service would strongly disagree. But, if you took advantage of modern marketing techniques and you optimized your manufacturing process, you might be able to make this a viable business.

speaker: Penny
text: And you know about that stuff?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Penny.
